clue.text: French and African soldiers turn around to face trouble

indicators.note: the soldiers stand around the French word, so it goes inside them

parts.note: an impi is a body of Zulu warriors
et is French for and
a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Foreign troops wheel about to confront some unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts ET inside IMPI, then GO follows; 'to face' is a link. 'Trouble' is used in the medical sense of an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetigo is a contagious skin infection, the kind of complaint called a skin trouble.

clue.text: Inactivity shown by one with detached retina

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the letters of retina have come loose and resettle in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone with a detached retina has to lie still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detached' rearranges RETINA into NERTIA; 'shown by' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is sluggishness, a lack of movement or action.

clue.text: Partiality for one novel weak- France Fr ness

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Partiality for one novel weak- France Fr ness': stray print ('France Fr') breaks 'weakness', so the second definition (one weakness in a novel's title, Pride and Prejudice) cannot be quoted as one run
annotationWithheld.clue: Partiality for one novel weak- France Fr ness

clue.text: Throw over the prize and we'll get drunk!

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: to toss is to throw
a pot is a trophy cup, a prize

explanation.surface: Fling the trophy aside and let's go on a bender!
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts TOSS above POT in the down entry; 'the' and 'and we'll get' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosspot is an old word for a habitual heavy drinker.

clue.text: Father Gerontius, forsaken by us, goes mad

indicators.note: the letters of us are abandoned from the name
going mad scrambles the remaining letters

explanation.surface: Father Gerontius, deserted by his flock, loses his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forsaken by us' removes US from GERONTIUS, and 'goes mad' rearranges GERONTI. Gerontius is the hero of Newman's poem and Elgar's oratorio.
explanation.definitionFit: A genitor is a biological parent, specifically the male one who begets offspring.

clue.text: Hear a genuine wrinkle

indicators.note: we are told to listen, so the word for genuine is taken by its sound

parts.note: pukka is Anglo-Indian slang for genuine or first-class

explanation.surface: Listen to a real crease in the fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent PUKKA and PUCKER sound alike; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To pucker is to gather into small folds, a synonym of wrinkle.

clue.text: Underwrite Roman island — Iberia, for example?

parts.note: to underwrite is to write one's name beneath, to pen it
insula is the Latin word for island

explanation.surface: Back a Roman isle, as Spain does?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Iberia as an example: Spain and Portugal sit on almost an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian landmass is a classic example of land nearly surrounded by sea.

clue.text: : Half-time break for the linesman Spain Pta

annotationWithheld.why: Held as ': Half-time break for the linesman Spain Pta': stray print (':' and 'Spain Pta') surrounds the clue, so the cryptic definition cannot be quoted as printed

clue.text: Introductions made by outdated USA S radio characters

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Introductions made by outdated USA S radio characters': stray print 'USA S' sits inside the wordplay (EX + anagram of RADIO), so the pieces cannot be quoted as one run
annotationWithheld.clue: Introductions made by outdated USA S radio characters

clue.text: Old mysteries, for use in alien form

definitions.note: the clue names the ancient rites; the answer is the adjective attached to them

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new form, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: Ancient secrets adapted for an outsider's use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges USE IN ALIEN; 'for' is a link. The definition stands for the rites of Eleusis, near Athens, whose name the answer gives.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eleusinian Mysteries were secret initiation rites of ancient Greece held at Eleusis.

clue.text: Antony's friend's sore back

indicators.note: back means the word sore is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Mark Antony's companion has a painful back.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after friend is 'is', a link. In Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra, Eros is Antony's faithful attendant who kills himself rather than kill his master.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare gives Antony a loyal servant called Eros in Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: How Duncan's angelic virtues would plead

definitions.text: How Duncan's angelic virtues would plead

parts.words: How Duncan's angelic virtues would plead
parts.note: Macbeth fears that the murdered King Duncan's virtues will plead like angels with the loud voice of a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A quotation question about Macbeth's victim.
explanation.walkthrough: From Macbeth I.7: Duncan's 'virtues will plead like angels, trumpet-tongued, against the deep damnation of his taking-off'.
explanation.definitionFit: The compound describes speaking with a loud, proclaiming voice, as Shakespeare says the virtues would.

clue.text: An old way to the peak for the birdman

parts.note: via is the Latin word for road, as in Roman roads
a tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: An ancient route up to the summit for a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the' is a link. TOR is a rocky hill in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdman is a jocular old word for a flyer of aircraft, a pilot.

clue.text: Free entry to this medieval village strip show

parts.note: open means free to all
the field is the whole entry for a race or contest

explanation.surface: Admission costs nothing for this old-time striptease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to this' is a link. 'strip show' plays on the medieval open-field system, where village land was farmed in strips.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval villages farmed undivided common land in narrow strips, the system named open-field.

clue.text: Kind of victory a coward 'may get?

explanation.surface: What sort of win could a coward achieve?
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe before 'may' is a printing blemish. A one-sided win is called a runaway victory, and a coward's way out is to run away.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-sided, easy win is described as runaway; fleeing from danger, what a coward may do, is running away.

clue.text: Fur-coated glutton

parts.note: glutton is the old name for a furry carnivore of the northern forests, not a greedy person in a fur coat

explanation.surface: A greedy eater wrapped in a fur.
explanation.walkthrough: Glutton is another name for this animal, the largest land member of the weasel family.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal, a stocky weasel relative of the far north, was traditionally called the glutton for its voracity.

clue.text: Soft-pedal criticism before there is a scene

parts.note: the soft pedal belongs to the piano, and p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
a review is a critical assessment

explanation.surface: Toning down critical comments before a fuss is made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft-pedal' looks like a verb meaning tone down; it gives P, the musical abbreviation for piano (soft).
explanation.definitionFit: A preview is a showing of a film or play to an audience ahead of its public opening.

clue.text: One of those paid by polite visitors in particular

definitions.text: One of those paid by polite visitors

explanation.surface: Courteous callers offer theirs, especially.
explanation.walkthrough: Visitors pay their respects; 'in' is a link, since 'in this respect' means 'in this particular'.
explanation.definitionFit: Callers pay courtesies called respects; a respect is also a detail or point, as in every particular.

clue.text: Bloomer in part of speech by girl

parts.note: a verb is one of the parts of speech
Ena is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl makes a blunder in her grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a mistake, but here it is a flowering plant; 'in' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena is a garden flower, and anything that flowers can be called a bloomer.

clue.text: Roman virgin queen, though very fast

definitions.text: Roman virgin queen, though very fast

parts.words: Roman virgin queen, though very fast
parts.note: Virgil's Aeneid tells of a warrior maiden queen of the Volsci so swift she could run over corn without bending it; fast also hints at loose morals

explanation.surface: A chaste ruler who was nonetheless rather fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Camilla in Virgil's Aeneid is a virgin warrior queen famed for speed; 'fast' plays on the sense of promiscuous against 'virgin'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Volscian queen of the Aeneid, a virgin warrior famously fleet of foot, bears this name.

clue.text: Millions enjoy its rays all the year round

definitions.text: Millions enjoy its rays all the year round

parts.words: Millions enjoy its rays all the year round
parts.note: not sunshine: the rays are the electron beams of the tube in a television set watched by millions

explanation.surface: A sun that shines for everyone in every season.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the sun; the rays are those of the tube in an old TV set.
explanation.definitionFit: Old television sets formed their pictures with beams from this negative electrode, which millions watched daily.

clue.text: Woman after dim: upbringing helps with deliveries

indicators.note: the woman comes after the turned word
in a down clue, bringing up the word dim turns it upwards, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a wife is a woman

explanation.surface: A woman follows a slow-witted man; her upbringing helps with chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upbringing' turns DIM into MID, and 'after' places WIFE behind it. The definition is a verb: to midwife is to assist a birth.
explanation.definitionFit: To midwife a baby is to assist at its birth, the delivery.

clue.text: This is sure to be revealed when it comes to name calling

definitions.text: This is sure to be revealed when it comes to name calling

parts.words: This is sure to be revealed when it comes to name calling
parts.note: name calling here is a roll call, where a missing person is exposed when nobody answers

explanation.surface: Abuse always brings something to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'name calling' suggests insults; it is a register being read out.
explanation.definitionFit: At a roll call, someone not being there is found out when their name gets no reply.

clue.text: Mountain goat's quality may-be sensed after a certain distance

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the certain distance

parts.note: sure means certain
a foot is a unit of distance

indicators.note: maybe signals that the letters could be otherwise arranged

explanation.surface: A goat's sure step might be felt only after some way has been covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may-be' rearranges SENSED into EDNESS, which goes 'after' SURE FOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountain goats are noted for steady footing on steep rock, never stumbling.

clue.text: Sounds as if it's sure to happen at a charity do

indicators.note: the words tell us to take the next word by its pronunciation

parts.note: fate is what is destined, sure to happen

explanation.surface: Something inevitable occurs at a fundraiser.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech FETE is pronounced like FATE. A fete is an outdoor fundraising fair with stalls, common in English villages; 'at a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fair held to raise money for a cause.

clue.text: Our envoi is broadcast widely by this agency

definitions.text: Our envoi is broadcast widely by this agency

indicators.note: broadcast scatters the letters widely, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: A sign-off sent out across Europe by a TV network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges OUR ENVOI IS; the whole clue also describes the network sharing programmes across Europe. An envoi is a closing stanza or farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurovision is the European Broadcasting Union's network for relaying television programmes between countries.

clue.text: Maroon filament

explanation.definitionFit: To maroon someone is to leave them stranded, abandoned; a filament is a single thread or fibre.

clue.text: Low-down woman unseen in the middle of a Swiss city

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, the low-down
Eve, the first woman

indicators.note: only the central letters of unseen are taken

explanation.surface: Secret facts about a woman nobody sees in a Swiss town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the middle' takes SE from UNSEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Genevese describes people or things belonging to Geneva, Switzerland's lakeside city.
